ages.label: Seniors 65+
ages.stat: Japan: 59.2% of special-fraud losses. Australia: 26.5% of losses vs 17.1% of population.
ages.scams: Digital arrest, bank/KYC, relative in trouble, romance

ages.label: Young adults 18-29
ages.stat: Singapore: ages 20-29 most affected by e-commerce, phishing and job scams; job scams cost S$123.5M (13.5% of losses).
ages.scams: Job/task, fake seller, investment, loan apps

ages.label: Teens 13-17
ages.stat: Australia (AIC 2025, n=1,953): 11.3% of adolescents experienced sexual extortion; over half before age 16.

complaint_mix_source: Superkalam summary of 2025 complaint categories (secondary source; treat as indicative)

avoidable.conservative_basis: NAB (Australia): real-time in-app scam prompts led customers to abandon 12% of flagged payments.
avoidable.ceiling_basis: Nottingham CEDEX lab experiment: confirm-the-action friction cut fraudulent payments by up to 94% (warnings alone: 18%). Lab setting, not real-world.

speed_matters.text: India's 1930 / CFCFRMS rapid-reporting system had helped save ~₹8,189 crore by Dec 2025 (₹11,158 crore by Jun 2026). Singapore recovered only ~15% of 2025 losses after the fact, so prevention beats recovery.

precedent: More than 280 Japanese financial institutions lowered elderly customers' ATM limits at police request.
